strengths: Correctly identifies the B-cell lineage using CD79A, IGKV5-2, CD37 and PTPRC
Recognizes activation-associated genes CD69, RGS1 and BIRC3
weaknesses: Broad label omits the supported activation state
Marker list is noisy with housekeeping/structural genes; subtype speculation is somewhat overconfident

strengths: Retains the correct B-cell lineage markers and adds a supported activation state (CD69, RGS1, BIRC3)
Maps to the conserved CL:0000236 B-cell ontology anchor
weaknesses: The 'mature' component is not strongly supported in the absence of robust CD19/MS4A1/CD27 evidence
Same noisy marker-list issue as CASSIA

clusterProfiler.predicted_cell_type: Medullary thymic epithelial cell / Not a typical lung immune cell; B-cell-like transcriptional signature with epithelial stress and viral response
strengths: Correctly acknowledges the presence of B-cell markers CD79A and IGKV5-2
Appropriately reports low confidence and absence of canonical mature B-cell markers
weaknesses: Proposes medullary thymic epithelial cell without any direct mTEC-specific marker (e.g., AIRE, FEZF2) and in a lung tissue context
Relies on non-specific structural/transport genes (COL27A1, SDC3, HYDIN) and generic metabolic enrichment
Ignores the dominant B-lineage positive evidence

supporting: CD79A and IGKV5-2 are B-lineage-specific markers
CD37 and PTPRC further support B-cell identity
Activation state is supported by CD69, RGS1, BIRC3 and CREM
Absence of T/NK/myeloid lineage markers supports a dominant B-cell identity
Retrieved literature PMID 37397988 is consistent with the B-lineage interpretation
conflicting: COL27A1, SDC3, HYDIN, RPE65, CRCT1 and glycosaminoglycan metabolism enrichment are non-B-cell signals likely representing ambient/low-specificity contamination
Absence of robust mature B-cell markers (CD19, MS4A1, CD27) weakens the 'mature' subtyping

enrichment terms were non-lineage-specific and not used as primary evidence
